## 2. Code Quality (decisions)

### Issue 4 [P1] (confidence: 9/10) PLAN.md:11-13 — retry envelope duplicated across 5 workers
**Decision: 4A (approved).** Extract one `withRetry(policy, handler)` wrapper
in a shared module (e.g. `jobs/retry/withRetry`) before touching any worker,
then convert all 5 workers to thin call sites in this PR. The wrapper owns:
error classification (retryable vs terminal), attempt logging, ledger write
(decision 2A), and hand-off to the library retry hook (decision 1A). Workers
own only their handler body. Order: wrapper + tests first, then workers one
commit each (structural change, then behavioral change; never both at once).

```
  worker file (x5)                shared module (x1)
  ┌────────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
  │ export default     │         │ withRetry(policy, handler)       │
  │   withRetry(       │ ──────► │   try handler(job)               │
  │     policy,        │         │   catch e:                       │
  │     handleXJob)    │         │     classify(e) → terminal|retry │
  └────────────────────┘         │     ledger.record(job, attempt)  │
                                 │     terminal → throw Unrecoverable│
                                 │     retry    → rethrow (library) │
                                 └──────────────────────────────────┘
                                 backoffStrategy(attempt) → delayMs (1A/3A)
```

## 3. Tests

Test framework: none detectable in this repo (only PLAN.md and CLAUDE.md are
checked in). Coverage diagram produced; concrete test file names use the
`*.test.ts` convention as a placeholder and must match the real repo.

### REGRESSION (mandatory, CRITICAL, no approval needed)
`processWebhookJob()` is rewritten (PLAN.md:16-17). Its prior at-most-once
behavior is existing behavior with no planned test. Per the regression rule
this test is added as a critical requirement:

- **`processWebhookJob.regression.test`** — given a receiver that returns 2xx
  then the connection drops before the response is read (or the worker crashes
  after a 2xx), assert the receiver observes exactly one delivery with the
  same `X-Webhook-Event-Id` on any second attempt, and the ledger shows one
  `delivered` row. Also assert that a 4xx (≠429) response produces exactly one
  attempt and no retry. This pins the new contract: at-least-once with a
  stable dedupe key, never a second *distinct* event.

### Coverage diagram

```
CODE PATHS                                              USER / OPERATOR FLOWS
[+] jobs/retry/backoffStrategy                          [+] Webhook receiver
  ├── [GAP] attempt 0..n → delay within [0, cap]          ├── [GAP] [→E2E] transient 5xx then 2xx: one event id, delivered
  ├── [GAP] delay never exceeds maxDelayMs                ├── [GAP] [→E2E] 4xx: single attempt, marked rejected
  ├── [GAP] jitter: two calls same attempt differ         └── [CRITICAL] [→E2E] 2xx then timeout: no duplicate event (regression)
  └── [GAP] attempt ≥ maxAttempts → -1 / terminal
[+] jobs/retry/withRetry                                [+] Operator
  ├── [GAP] handler succeeds → no ledger failure row       ├── [GAP] job exhausts → lands in DLQ, alert fires once
  ├── [GAP] retryable error → ledger row + rethrow         ├── [GAP] job older than maxAge → stops retrying, DLQ
  ├── [GAP] terminal error → Unrecoverable, no retry       └── [GAP] replay from DLQ → new attempt chain, same event id
  ├── [GAP] classify(): timeout / conn reset / 5xx / 429
  ├── [GAP] classify(): 4xx ≠ 429 / validation / unknown
  └── [GAP] ledger write fails → retry still scheduled, error logged
[+] jobs/retry/policy
  └── [GAP] defaults + per-worker override validation
[+] workers/* (x5)
  └── [GAP] each worker: handler invoked via withRetry with expected policy
[+] webhook ledger
  ├── [GAP] one row per attempt, monotonically increasing attempt
  └── [GAP] concurrent duplicate job for same event id → single delivery

COVERAGE: 0/20 paths tested (0%)  |  Code paths: 0/14  |  Flows: 0/6
QUALITY: none yet  |  GAPS: 20 (3 E2E, 1 CRITICAL regression, 0 eval)
```
